title: Degree as a multiplicity-weighted sum over integral components
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ be the irreducible components of dimension one [def-weil-irreducible-components], each equipped with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure (on an affine open this is the quotient by the prime ideal of the component) [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is a finite list; each $C_i$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ of dimension one. Let $\xi_i$ be its generic point, meaning $\overline{\{\xi_i\}}=C_i$, and put $m_i=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i})$, using the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and module length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Each $m_i$ is a finite positive integer. Write $\mathcal N|_{C_i}=j_i^*\mathcal N$ for pullback along the closed immersion $j_i:C_i\to X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. With $\deg_k(\mathcal P)=\chi(Y,\mathcal P)-\chi(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ on any proper $Y/k$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic], one has
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\sum_{i=1}^t m_i\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i}).$$
The sum is zero when $t=0$, including when $X$ is empty or has dimension at most zero.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components, rank-one specialization; multiplicity definition immediately before the lemma.

proof.text: First establish the Noetherian and coherence hypotheses. A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal, both finitely generated. Thus the one-point affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian. Properness includes finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. The structure module is quasi-coherent and locally generated by $1$, and $\mathcal N$ is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank one. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] both are coherent. The same reasoning applies to any proper $k$-scheme below. Tensoring a coherent module by $\mathcal N$ preserves coherence: on a trivializing open of $\mathcal N$ the tensor is that coherent module itself. Euler characteristics of all these coherent modules on proper schemes are defined by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined].

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; coherent.tex Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; hypotheses for varieties.tex Tag 0AYW

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] there are only finitely many irreducible components, hence finitely many of dimension one. Give each such component $C_i$ its reduced induced structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its dimension is one by its selection, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes it proper over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] it has the unique generic point $\xi_i$ specified in the statement. The affine description of the reduced induced structure is the quotient by the radical ideal of the component, which is prime because the component is irreducible.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, preliminary multiplicity paragraph and beginning of proof; schemes.tex Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] to the coherent module $\mathcal O_X$ on the Noetherian scheme $X$. Obtain a finite filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal F_s=\mathcal O_X$ by coherent submodules, with quotients $\mathcal Q_a=\mathcal F_a/\mathcal F_{a-1}\cong(j_a)_*\mathcal I_a$, where $j_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow X$ is an integral closed subscheme and $\mathcal I_a\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_a}$ is a nonzero coherent ideal. Every $Z_a$ is proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and therefore Noetherian by Step 1. The coherent filtration is the common device used below to calculate both the degree and its generic multiplicities.

source.place: Tag 01YF, lemma-coherent-filter, applied to the structure module; agent-written devissage of varieties.tex Tag 0AYW

proof.text: Every $Z_a$ has dimension zero or one: a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $Z_a$ is a chain in $X$. If $\dim Z_a=1$, its underlying set must be an irreducible component of $X$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] the irreducible set $Z_a$ lies in some irreducible component $T$ of $X$, which is closed. If $Z_a\neq T$, it lies properly inside $T$, and a strict chain $T_0\subsetneq Z_a$ witnessing dimension one would give $T_0\subsetneq Z_a\subsetneq T$, contradicting $\dim X\leq1$. Hence its underlying set is some $C_i$. An integral scheme is reduced, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies $Z_a$ with $C_i$ over $X$. If $\dim Z_a=0$, then every point has closure equal to $Z_a$: a smaller nonempty irreducible closed closure would give a chain of length one. Uniqueness of generic points then says that $Z_a$ is a single point.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, reduction to integral one-dimensional supports; elementary chain argument from the definition of dimension

proof.text:
Fix $i$. Take stalks of the filtration at $\xi_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks], $(\mathcal Q_a)_{\xi_i}=0$ if $\xi_i\notin Z_a$. If $\xi_i\in Z_a$, closedness implies $C_i=\overline{\{\xi_i\}}\subseteq Z_a$; maximal irreducibility of $C_i$ implies $Z_a=C_i$ as sets, hence as reduced closed subschemes by Step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk], $(\mathcal I_a)_{\xi_i}=\mathcal O_{C_i,\xi_i}=\kappa(\xi_i)$. Its pushforward stalk is this residue field regarded as a module over $R_i=\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}$. It has length one: since $j_a$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $\mathcal O_X\to(j_a)_*\mathcal O_{C_i}$ is surjective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] the stalk map $R_i\to\mathcal O_{C_i,\xi_i}=\kappa(\xi_i)$ is surjective and the action factors through $R_i\twoheadrightarrow\kappa(\xi_i)$, so its only submodules are zero and itself. Repeated use of [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact], starting with the zero stalk, gives
$$m_i=\operatorname{length}_{R_i}R_i=\#\{a:Z_a=C_i\}.$$
This proves finiteness. It also proves positivity: $R_i$ has the nonzero residue field $\kappa(\xi_i)$, so its length is not zero. Thus every multiplicity in the statement is a finite positive integer.

source.place: Tag 01YF, filtration localized at a generic point; algebra.tex Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive; generic multiplicities as in varieties.tex Tag 0AYW

proof.text:
For a coherent module $\mathcal G$ on $X$ write $D(\mathcal G)=\chi(X,\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal G)-\chi(X,\mathcal G)$. Tensoring the filtration sequences by the finite locally free module $\mathcal N$ is exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. Both the original and tensor sequences consist of coherent modules, by Step 1. Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to each pair of sequences and subtract to obtain $D(\mathcal F_a)=D(\mathcal F_{a-1})+D(\mathcal Q_a)$. Since $D(0)=0$, finite induction gives
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=D(\mathcal O_X)=\sum_{a=1}^s D(\mathcal Q_a).$$
Here $\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal N$, with the map $n\otimes f\mapsto fn$, and degree is [def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

source.place: Tag 0AYW, tensoring the coherent filtration and Euler characteristic additivity; lemma-euler-characteristic-additive; coherent.tex Tag 01YF

proof.text:
For the closed immersion $j_a$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\mathcal N\otimes(j_a)_*\mathcal I_a\cong(j_a)_*(j_a^*\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal I_a).$$
Indeed, the map sends $n\otimes s$ to $j_a^*n\otimes s$. On an open set where $e$ generates $\mathcal N$, both sides identify with $(j_a)_*\mathcal I_a$ and the map is the identity under $e\otimes s\mapsto s$. Replacing $e$ by $ue$, for a unit $u$, multiplies both identifications by the same unit, so these local inverses agree and glue. This proves the comparison here without any flatness assumption on $j_a$.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, tensor identification for closed-subscheme modules; rank-one local calculation

proof.text:
The cohomology in the Euler characteristics is computed in $\mathcal O$-modules; by [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree], on $Z_a$ and on $X$ it agrees, naturally in module maps, with the cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaves. Apply [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] to the underlying abelian sheaves of $\mathcal I_a$ and $j_a^*\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal I_a$. Its hypotheses hold because a closed immersion identifies the underlying space with a closed subset. The cohomology isomorphisms are $k$-linear: their naturality applied to multiplication by every $b\in k$ makes them commute with scalar multiplication. Their finite-dimensional cohomology groups and finite Euler sums are justified by Step 1. Combining them with Step 7 yields
$$D(\mathcal Q_a)=\chi(Z_a,j_a^*\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal I_a)-\chi(Z_a,\mathcal I_a).$$

source.place: Tag 02UV, lemma-cohomology-and-closed-immersions; application to the filtration factors of coherent.tex Tag 01YF

proof.text:
Suppose $\dim Z_a=1$, so $Z_a=C_i$ for a unique $i$. The pullback $\mathcal N|_{C_i}$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1). The nonzero coherent ideal $\mathcal I_a$ has generic stalk equal to $\kappa(\xi_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk], and thus generic rank one. The integral proper dimension-one scheme $C_i$, invertible module $\mathcal N|_{C_i}$ and coherent module $\mathcal I_a$ meet all hypotheses of [lem-trf-curve-euler-tensor-generic-rank]. Its formula, with $r=1$, and Step 8 give
$$D(\mathcal Q_a)=\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i}).$$
This uses no smoothness, normality, or algebraic closedness of $k$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, n=r=1; the integral-curve input of Tag 0AYW

proof.text: If $\dim Z_a=0$, Step 4 makes $Z_a$ a one-point scheme. A Zariski trivializing neighborhood of its unique point is all of $Z_a$. Since $j_a^*\mathcal N$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1), choose a generator $e$ globally on $Z_a$. The maps $e\otimes s\mapsto s$ and $s\mapsto e\otimes s$ give inverse isomorphisms $j_a^*\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal I_a\cong\mathcal I_a$. Consequently the two Euler characteristics in Step 8 agree, so $D(\mathcal Q_a)=0$.

source.place: Zero-dimensional term in the devissage for Tag 0AYW; rank-one trivialization, cf. lemma-chi-tensor-finite

proof.text:
Group the finite sum of Step 6 by its integral supports. By Steps 9 and 10, only the $Z_a=C_i$ contribute; by Step 5 there are exactly $m_i$ such factors. Thus
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\sum_a D(\mathcal Q_a)=\sum_{i=1}^t\#\{a:Z_a=C_i\}\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i})=\sum_{i=1}^t m_i\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i}).$$
If $t=0$, every filtration factor has dimension zero and its contribution is zero. For $X=\varnothing$, the structure module is zero and the Euler sums are zero; one can take the length-zero filtration. Hence the asserted empty-sum convention holds in all the stated edge cases.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, conclusion; finite sum regrouping of the coherent filtration calculation

This replaces the source proof's preliminary component separation and nilpotence induction by the existing general coherent filtration, below the fixed unit route.
